statement_frozen: For any graph H is there some c=c(H)>0 such that every graph G on n vertices that does not contain H as an induced subgraph contains either a complete graph or independent set on >= n^c vertices?

conventions.induced: closed under both edges and non-edges
conventions.h_H(n): min{ hom(G) : G on n vertices, H induced-free } (minimum always attained; feasible set nonempty for every n>=1)
conventions.complement_bar: H-bar denotes graph complement; F1: induced subgraphs of H-free are H-free; F2: homogeneous sets of induced subgraphs are homogeneous in the host; F3: cliques of G <-> independent sets of G-bar; F4: h_H nondecreasing in n

parameter_space.H_universe: the six receipt H's (2K2, P3, 3K1, claw K1,3, C4, K2) plus the F7 family {K1, K2, Kbar2=2K1, P3, Pbar3, K3, Kbar3=3K1} — all graphs on <= 3 vertices plus the four key 4-vertex H's (2K2, claw, C4, P4 as the honest continuation front)
parameter_space.substitution_frame: uniform blow-ups H1[H2], q,s in {1,2,3}^2 exhaustive, sampled beyond

acceptance_criteria: AC-1: every h-table value in solution.json must be re-derived by at least two independent methods (exhaustive/targeted enumeration + z3 SAT/UNSAT dual certificates) with exact agreement

AC-2: the P3 classification (P3-free <=> disjoint union of cliques) must hold on every P3-free graph enumerated exhaustively at n<=6, and the sharp law h_P3(n)=ceil(sqrt(n)) must hold at n<=7 exhaustively with witnesses at n<=30
AC-3: the 3K1 law h_3K1(n) >= t_n := min{t : t(t+1)>=n} must hold at n<=7 exhaustively, with the C5 honesty correction encoded (hom >= sqrt(n) REAL-VALUED IS FALSE at n=5)
AC-4: Ramsey cross-check R(3,3)=6: every 6-vertex graph has omega>=3 or alpha>=3 (exhaustive)

AC-5: the substitution identities and avoidance table must be verified by brute isomorphism; the blow-up law hom(G) >= min(h_H1(q), h_H2(s)) must hold on the full exhaustive frame with zero violations
AC-6: the exponent law f(c1,c2)=c1c2/(c1+c2) and the multi-level harmonic law F_k=(sum 1/ci)^{-1} must verify in exact rational arithmetic

AC-7: the F7 family theorem finite core: for every H in {K2, 2K1, P3, Pbar3, K3, 3K1} and n<=7, every H-free graph has hom >= floor(sqrt(n)) (exhaustive), and the tightness witness (disjoint union of 2^j copies of K_{2^j} on n=4^j vertices, max(omega,alpha)=2^j=floor(sqrt(n))) must verify exactly for j=1..3
AC-8: negative controls: a corrupted table value, a corrupted witness, and a corrupted classification instance must each be REJECTED (comparator non-vacuity)
